description: Between You Two V2 relationship-first headline/move and shared-Moon rows. Bond headline/move approvals are direction-specific so unseen reverse-direction wording cannot inherit owner approval.

rows.body: The silence may be hitting an old insecurity before you have new information.
Wait for the new information before you decide what the delay means.
{{holder1}} may be reading the delay through an old insecurity.
If the delay is ordinary, say that clearly before {{holder1}} has to guess.
You may be agreeing before you check the cost.
Check the money, time, and logistics before you agree to one more thing.
{{holder1}} may be agreeing before they check the cost.
Check the money, time, and logistics before you ask {{holder1}} to add one more thing.
You have been agreeing longer than you actually wanted to.
Say no to the plan before irritation has to say it for you.
{{holder1}} may have been agreeing longer than they actually wanted to.
Take the first no seriously instead of waiting for {{holder1}} to get sharper.
Being kept waiting is starting to feel like disrespect.
Acknowledge that you were left waiting before the argument becomes about everything the delay supposedly means.
{{holder1}} may be reading the delay as disrespect.
Acknowledge the delay before you defend why it happened.
You may be reacting to the tone more than the message.
Answer what was actually said before you start arguing with the tone.
{{holder1}} may be reacting to the tone more than the message.
If your reply was brief, make the meaning clear before {{holder1}} has to guess.
A bad day is making a small disappointment land harder.
Handle the immediate disappointment before you argue about the size of the reaction.
{{holder1}} may be reacting from a harder day than you can see.
Handle the immediate disappointment before you argue about the size of the reaction.
You may be filling the silence with a problem that has not happened.
Ask the question before you start responding to the explanation you made up.
{{holder1}} may be filling the silence with a problem that has not happened.
If you are simply busy or delayed, say that before {{holder1}} has to invent the reason.
They may put an unfamiliar option in front of you before you feel ready.
Find out what the option actually requires before nervousness decides for you.
You may put an unfamiliar option in front of {{holder1}} before they feel ready.
Give {{holder1}} enough information to consider the option without pushing for an immediate answer.
The part that hurts is how little say you had.
Ask for the information or decision you were left out of instead of fighting about the answer after it is already final.
{{holder1}} may be reacting to how little say they had.
Put the information and decision on the table before asking {{holder1}} to accept the outcome.
The plan is becoming your job.
Decide who is actually handling the next step before you make another plan.
{{holder1}} may be carrying more of the follow-through.
Decide who is actually handling the next step before you make another plan.
You are slipping back into the old job you used to do in this relationship.
Notice which job you picked up automatically before you keep doing it.
{{holder1}} may be slipping back into the old role they used to take with you.
Ask instead of letting the old division of work restart by default.
Their recognition may be making your contribution disappear.
Name what you contributed instead of pretending the missing credit does not matter.
Your recognition may be making {{holder1}}'s contribution disappear.
Give {{holder1}} specific credit for the part they actually did.
Their last-minute changes are costing you time.
Before you adjust again, count how much of your day has already been rearranged around their changes.
Your last-minute changes may be costing {{holder1}} time.
Before you change the plan again, check what {{holder1}} already rearranged around it.
You can understand why they are unavailable and still feel disappointed.
Say you wanted more time without turning their schedule into a rejection.
{{holder1}} may understand why you are unavailable and still feel disappointed.
Say what you can actually give instead of leaving {{holder1}} to guess.
You may be able to finish the vulnerable part without defending it.
Let the explanation finish before you start solving or correcting it.
{{holder1}} may be able to say more because they do not have to defend the reaction.
Let {{holder1}} finish before you explain why they should see it differently.
They may bring you an opportunity that actually fits your life.
Follow the lead if it connects to something you already wanted.
You may bring them an opportunity that actually fits their life.
Pass it along if it connects to something {{holder1}} already wanted.
You can say what you actually want before resentment does it for you.
Give the clear answer first instead of choosing the easiest plan to agree to.
{{holder1}} may tell you what they actually want before resentment builds.
Take the clear answer seriously, even if it is less convenient.
You can get more done together than either of you wants to do alone.
Pick the task you have both been postponing and finish it together.
You can get more done together than either of you wants to do alone.
Pick the task you have both been postponing and finish it together.
The conversation may finally come out cleanly.
Say the part you mean and stop before you turn it into five more paragraphs.
{{holder1}} may be easier to understand without a second round of explanation.
Take the clear answer at face value instead of pulling for a hidden meaning.
They may notice what you need before you have to spell it out.
Let them help in the specific way they already noticed.
You may notice what {{holder1}} needs before they have to ask.
Offer the specific thing you can see {{holder1}} needs.
One off day can stay one off day.
Leave the imperfect sentence where it is unless there is actually something to clarify.
A clumsy moment does not have to become a larger problem between you.
Do not over-explain a clumsy sentence that {{holder1}} already understood.
They may introduce you to something new without forcing a big decision.
Try the first step if it interests you. You can decide the rest later.
You may introduce {{holder1}} to something new without asking them to decide the whole future.
Offer the first step without turning it into a commitment {{holder1}} has not made.
You may finally be able to name what has been uneven.
Name the money, decision, or responsibility that is actually uneven instead of arguing about the relationship in general.
{{holder1}} may finally tell you where the arrangement has felt uneven.
Listen for the specific imbalance {{holder1}} is naming before you defend the whole arrangement.
You have evidence that they will follow through.
Let the follow-through count instead of checking one more time.
{{holder1}} has evidence that you will follow through.
Do what you said you would do without making {{holder1}} chase the answer.
The old rhythm may feel good even if one part no longer fits.
Keep the part of the routine you still like and change the part that no longer fits.
{{holder1}} may fall into an old role because it still feels easy.
Do not assume the familiar role still works for {{holder1}} just because it comes easily.
They may give you the credit without making you ask for it.
Let the specific recognition land instead of brushing past it.
You may be able to give {{holder1}} the credit without making them ask for it.
Name the part {{holder1}} did well instead of giving a vague compliment.
A different plan may suit you better than the usual one.
Say yes to the change if the usual plan was already feeling repetitive.
A different plan may give {{holder1}} the break they were already ready for.
Offer the different option without making it a test of how spontaneous {{holder1}} can be.
The small effort matters because it was specific to you.
Notice the specific effort instead of measuring it by how big it was.
The small effort matters because it was specific to {{holder1}}.
Do the small thing you already know would make {{holder1}}'s day easier.

rows.body_you: You may both have less patience for delays today.

rows.body_you: The Moon is in a fire sign and aspecting both charts today, so both of you may be quicker to act and less patient with delays. A changed plan or blunt reply can become more irritating than it usually would. Say what changed before either of you decides why the other person did it.
